text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Prime minister designate Mart Siimann announced that he will end negotiations with political parties and will form a minority government as the differences between possible partners could not be overcome.
- President Lennart Meri presented the country's highest order to former German foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher.
- The Coalition Party, Centre Party and Reform Party agreed that Toomas Savi will be re-elected chairman of the parliament.
- The official representative of Chechnya in Estonia called for official recognition of Chechnya as an independent state by Estonia.
SONUMILEHT
- The decree of the defence forces commander on allowing sportsmen to practice during army service has resulted in an increasing number of athletes signing up.
- Every 10th child receives once a year an injury requiring medical assistance, the Tallinn social and health department announced.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin accused Estonia and Latvia of repressing the Russian-speaking population in his speech about the state of the country.
- 325 candidates competed on the tiny island of Saaremaa for two vacancies as bank tellers as the area suffers from high unemployment.
- Estonia and Latvia failed to reach an agreement on the volume of fishing in each other's territorial waters, although a fishery protocol was signed Wednesday.
- There are more than 45,000 firearm owners in Estonia.
POSTIMEES
- A memorial plaque to Juri Vilms, an Estonian politician executed by the Germans in Helsinki in 1918, was unveiled in the Finnish capital.
- The MRP private bus firm discussed their planned strike today but did not reach a decision.
ARIPAEV
- Ministries have proposed 16 development plans needing foreign loans. Finance ministry experts consider half of them feasible and tend to prefer infrastructure modernisation and development plans.

- There are plans to introduce a third ferry on the Tallinn-Helsinki route. The Silja Line will retire the Silja Festival ferry from April 1 and is to decide later, whether to bring another ferry to the line from autumn.
- The government proposes that the new price of oil shale be 106 kroons per tonne but the oil shale mining firm says will provide no profit.
